answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on shared resource allocations. The contract caps each bond’s influence and slashes it when a randomly audited claim proves fraudulent; honest agents recover theirs after a delay. A beacon can announce audit samples, while an atlas tracks bond histories and a relic marks a scarce resource under dispute. Creating sybils then requires locking more capital per unit of influence, and detected abuse destroys that capital.
